core_obligations: Read off from the ideal-sheaf description of closed subschemes that X -> X union Y and Y -> X union Y are closed immersions, and that X union Y and X cap Y are cut out by I cap J and I + J (proof lines 576-577).

Build the two maps of the displayed sequence of O_S-modules: the canonical maps O_{X union Y} -> O_X and O_{X union Y} -> O_Y for the first arrow, then the canonical map O_X -> O_{X cap Y} together with the negative of the canonical map O_Y -> O_{X cap Y} for the second arrow, and use the closed-immersion equivalence to view all of them as quasi-coherent O_S-modules (proof lines 578-586).

Verify exactness of 0 -> O_{X union Y} -> O_X x O_Y -> O_{X cap Y} -> 0 affine locally: on an affine open U = Spec(A) with X cap U and Y cap U cut out by ideals I and J, the union is cut out by I cap J and the intersection by I + J, so exactness is that of 0 -> A/(I cap J) -> A/I x A/J -> A/(I + J) -> 0 (proof lines 587-595).

Prove the diagram is cocartesian: given a scheme T and morphisms f : X -> T, g : Y -> T agreeing on X cap Y, construct the required h : X union Y -> T. The construction is local on X union Y; over a point s in X but not Y (resp. Y but not X) the inclusion X -> X union Y is an isomorphism near s, and over s in X cap Y one picks an affine open V = Spec(B) of T around f(s) = g(s) and an affine open U = Spec(A) of S with f(X cap U), g(Y cap U) contained in V, producing ring maps B -> A/I and B -> A/J that agree as maps into A/(I + J); the short exact sequence displayed above provides the unique lift to a ring map B -> A/(I cap J), which is the local description of h (proof lines 596-618).
proof_roadmap: Closed immersions X -> X union Y and Y -> X union Y, and the identification of the two ideal sheaves (proof lines 576-577).
Construction of the maps in the short exact sequence of structure sheaves, including the sign in the second map, and reduction of exactness to the affine ring statement (proof lines 578-595).

Construction of h : X union Y -> T by glueing, with the case analysis X minus Y, Y minus X and X cap Y, and the algebraic lift of the two agreeing ring maps along the exact sequence (proof lines 596-618).
difficulty_reason: The claim is that for two closed subschemes X, Y of a scheme S the union X union Y is the pushout of X and Y along their scheme theoretic intersection, and that the structure sheaves fit into 0 -> O_{X union Y} -> O_X x O_Y -> O_{X cap Y} -> 0 (statement lines 558-572). The proof has to do two genuinely different things: construct the four maps of that sequence, including the sign on O_Y -> O_{X cap Y}, and then solve the universal problem for an arbitrary test scheme T. The second part is the non-formal step: the author constructs h : X union Y -> T locally, splitting into the three regions of X union Y, and on the overlap X cap Y reduces the two agreeing morphisms f and g to ring maps B -> A/I and B -> A/J agreeing into A/(I + J), which the exact sequence lifts uniquely to B -> A/(I cap J) (proof lines 596-618). This is H2: a real local construction with a case analysis and an explicit algebraic lift, but no research-level input and no hypothesis beyond the definitions.
